notes:
I couldn't write these notes because my research tool stopped working before any pages loaded. My only attempt to fetch sources ended with a message that I had used up my research calls for this turn. No content came back, so I have nothing from the approved sites to work from.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point. Writing the commentary from memory would break that rule, so I haven't drafted any verse notes.

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll start with these pages:

- **Verse-by-verse:** enduringword.com (Psalm 80), plus Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com.
- **Other sources:** the preceptaustin.org Psalm 80 page and the netbible.org notes.
- **Early church:** Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org. His Bible numbered the Psalms differently, so this psalm is his Psalm 79 there.
- **Protestant traditions:** searches on spurgeon.org, desiringgod.org, ligonier.org, wesley.nnu.edu and others. These would look for real differences between traditions, for example over who "the man at Your right hand" is in v. 17.

You could also paste in text from any of these pages, and I'll write the notes using only that material, citing each point to its source.
